qualification: Documented and synthetically tested, not qualified on the instrument: built from published interface documentation and a survey of existing instrument drivers, and tested with synthetic messages only. Validate in the laboratory before clinical use.

connectors.label: HL7 MLLP: end block without carriage return
connectors.summary: For senders that end each frame with the end byte 0x1C alone. A carriage return that does follow is accepted. Output still ends 0x1C 0x0D.
connectors.evidence: Six surveyed instrument drivers end an incoming frame at 0x1C without waiting for 0x0D.

connectors.label: HL7 source answering orders with order responses
connectors.summary: Enhanced acknowledgement mode; OML^O33, OML^O35, OML^O21 and ORM^O01 are answered with a base HL7 order response (ORL or ORR) that holds MSH and MSA only. AA means the order was stored; it states no per-order acceptance (there is no ORC) and the reply is not an IHE LAW LAB-28 response. Other messages still get an ACK.
connectors.evidence: HL7 v2.5.1 chapter 4: the response group of ORL and ORR is optional, a response may hold only MSH and MSA. Documentation and synthetic tests only.

connectors.label: HL7 destination for order messages answered by order responses
connectors.summary: Accepts ACK, ORL and ORR as the acknowledgement of a sent order (OML/ORM), correlated by MSA-2 with the order's MSH-10. acknowledged reflects the MSA code only: per-order status in ORC-1 (for example OK or UA) is not evaluated. Without this setting an ORL answer is not recognised and the delivery times out.
connectors.evidence: Two surveyed instrument drivers take an ORL^O34 answer as the acknowledgement of an order and never read ORC-1.

connectors.label: ASTM source: specimen id in O-4, third component
connectors.summary: For instruments that carry the specimen number in the instrument specimen id (O-4, ^^123456^B). It becomes the message's sample id: searchable on the Messages page and part of the duplicate identity. Without it such a message is stored with no sample id.
connectors.evidence: Nine surveyed drivers of one hematology and coagulation instrument family read the specimen from O-4 component 3. Driver evidence only; the vendor specification was not read.

connectors.label: ASTM over TCP: long frames
connectors.summary: Frames of up to 64,000 text characters instead of 240, sent and accepted. Both sides must use the same size.
connectors.evidence: Hematology TCP interfaces document frames of about 64,000 characters; one LIS middleware driver makes the frame size configurable from 247 to 64,000.

connectors.label: ASTM: repeat ENQ before giving up
connectors.summary: Sends ENQ up to 7 times (a quiet or busy receiver) before the send is abandoned and retried by the delivery policy.
connectors.evidence: A published LIS middleware interface guide (Siemens Atellica Data Manager) sends ENQ again up to 7 times instead of EOT when the receiver does not reply within 15 seconds.

mappings.label: ASTM results to HL7 ORU^R01 (E1394 layout: test code in the 4th component)
mappings.summary: Patient, specimen and one OBX per result record. The test code is read from the 4th component of the universal test id (^^^Ferritin^1), the value from the first component of R-4, the reference range from R-6.
notes: Put your test codes in the tests table (code to the OBX-3 text, for example Ferritin to 2276-4^Ferritin^LN); a code that is not listed is kept as it is.
A message that holds several patients or orders (a batch upload) is refused with a transform error instead of mixing specimens; send results per sample.
Only the first component of the result value (R-4) is mapped. OBX-2 is NM for a plain number and ST for anything else.
Dates are copied as sent. Convert time zones with a datetime rule if the instrument's clock is not the lab's.

Fits the documented result upload of the Beckman Coulter Access/DxI interface (test code in R-3.4, replicate in R-3.5, reference range text in R-6, the interpretation text of R-4.2 is not carried) and the Roche Elecsys-type upload (code in R-3.4; its low^high range in R-6 is carried as 'low' only).
mappings.evidence: Beckman Coulter C03112-AF (UniCel DxI / Access 2 LIS Vendor Information), tables 3-2 to 3-5 and the typical upload messages; Roche cobas e 411 Host Interface Manual v2.2, result record. Fixture is synthetic.

mappings.label: ASTM results to HL7 ORU^R01 (cobas-type upload: code before the slash)
mappings.summary: For the cobas-type format of the Roche/Hitachi cobas e 411, whose universal test id is ^^^code/dilution/pre-dilution: the host test code before the first slash becomes OBX-3, the operator R-11 OBX-16 and the instrument id R-14 OBX-18.
notes: Put your test codes in the tests table (code to the OBX-3 text, for example Ferritin to 2276-4^Ferritin^LN); a code that is not listed is kept as it is.
A message that holds several patients or orders (a batch upload) is refused with a transform error instead of mixing specimens; send results per sample.
Only the first component of the result value (R-4) is mapped. OBX-2 is NM for a plain number and ST for anything else.
Dates are copied as sent. Convert time zones with a datetime rule if the instrument's clock is not the lab's.
R-9 status F (initial result) and C (rerun result) are copied; HL7 reads C as a corrected result.
Abnormal flags L, H, LL, HH, N, A are copied as sent; the instrument's LL and HH mean 'outside the measuring range', which HL7 table 0078 does not say.
A qualitative result arrives as a code (1 positive, 0 border line, -1 negative) in R-4; translate it per assay with a rule of your own.
mappings.evidence: Roche/Hitachi cobas e 411 Host Interface Manual v2.2 (Nov 2013), result record cobas-type format and the uploaded examples. Fixture is synthetic.

mappings.label: ASTM results to HL7 ORU^R01 (specimen id in O-4, test code in the 5th component)
mappings.summary: For instruments that put the specimen number in the instrument specimen id (O-4, third component: ^^123456^B) and the test code in the fifth component of the universal test id (^^^^WBC^1).
notes: Put your test codes in the tests table (code to the OBX-3 text, for example Ferritin to 2276-4^Ferritin^LN); a code that is not listed is kept as it is.
A message that holds several patients or orders (a batch upload) is refused with a transform error instead of mixing specimens; send results per sample.
Only the first component of the result value (R-4) is mapped. OBX-2 is NM for a plain number and ST for anything else.
Dates are copied as sent. Convert time zones with a datetime rule if the instrument's clock is not the lab's.

Set the source connector's sample_id_path to O.4.3 (connector profile astm_specimen_id_in_o4_component_3): the mapping reads the specimen there, but the stored message gets its sample id, its search entry and its duplicate identity from that setting.
mappings.evidence: Nine surveyed drivers of one hematology and coagulation instrument family read the specimen from O-4 component 3 and the analyte from R-3 component 5. The instrument vendor's specification was not read; the fixture is synthetic.

mappings.label: AU results to HL7 ORU^R01
mappings.summary: The sample id and one OBX per result item. The instrument's two-character flags are mapped through the flags table, which ships empty (nothing is mapped until you list the flags your instrument sends).
notes: The test codes of the instrument's parameter sheet (01, 02, ...) go in the tests table; an unlisted code is kept as it is.
Leading zeros of the instrument's fixed-width value are removed (005.50 becomes 5.50, 000.40 becomes 0.40); trailing zeros are kept.
Quality-control, calibration and reagent-blank messages are mapped too; use a channel filter on kind (normal, rerun, stat, stat_rerun) to send patient results only.
The sample input is the framed message exactly as the instrument sends it (start and end control bytes included), read with the source settings shown.
mappings.evidence: Fixed-width result message of the online parameter sheet (sample id and result items) as parsed by the AU codec; synthetic fixture.

mappings.label: HL7 ORM^O01 order to ASTM order download (Access/DxI layout)
mappings.summary: A patient record (id, name, birth date, sex) and one order record: specimen id from OBR-3, the tests of every OBR as ^^^code repeats, priority S or R, action code from ORC-1 (NW to A, CA to C), specimen type text from OBR-15.
notes: The message must be one patient, one specimen and one order: every OBR becomes a repetition of the universal test id of one order record (1 to 18 tests), and every OBR must carry the same specimen id, priority and order control. A message that is not (several patients or specimens, more than 18 tests, mixed values) is refused with a transform error, nothing is dropped or filtered.
Put your test codes in the tests table to translate the LIS code to the instrument's code; an unlisted code is sent as it is.

A priority other than S or R, an order control other than NW or CA, and an unlisted specimen type are left out; the instrument then uses its defaults (an unknown priority code would make it reject the order).
mappings.evidence: Beckman Coulter C03112-AF (UniCel DxI / Access 2 LIS Vendor Information), test order record: specimen id O-3, universal test id O-5 (fourth component, repeat delimiter supported), priority S or R, action code A, C or N, specimen type text; patient record P-3, P-6, P-8, P-9. Fixture is synthetic.

mappings.label: HL7 OML^O33 order to ASTM order download (Access/DxI layout)
mappings.summary: As the ORM preset for an OML^O33 order: specimen id from SPM-2 (entity identifier), specimen type from SPM-4, one order record with the tests of every OBR. It reads the IHE LAW layout of the order (SPM, OBR-4) only; it is not LAB-28 support.
notes: The message must be one patient, one specimen and one order: every OBR becomes a repetition of the universal test id of one order record (1 to 18 tests), and every OBR must carry the same specimen id, priority and order control. A message that is not (several patients or specimens, more than 18 tests, mixed values) is refused with a transform error, nothing is dropped or filtered.
Put your test codes in the tests table to translate the LIS code to the instrument's code; an unlisted code is sent as it is.
mappings.evidence: Beckman Coulter C03112-AF (UniCel DxI / Access 2 LIS Vendor Information), test order record: specimen id O-3, universal test id O-5 (fourth component, repeat delimiter supported), priority S or R, action code A, C or N, specimen type text; patient record P-3, P-6, P-8, P-9. Fixture is synthetic. The OML^O33 input layout (specimen in SPM, test in OBR-4) is the one IHE LAW describes; nothing else of LAW is implemented.

mappings.label: HL7 ORM^O01 order to ASTM order download (cobas-type layout)
mappings.summary: For the Roche/Hitachi cobas e 411 cobas-type format: a bare P record, one order record with the specimen id, the tests as ^^^code repeats, priority, collection time (14 digits), action code A, numeric specimen type (1 serum, 2 urine) and report type O.
notes: The message must be one patient, one specimen and one order: every OBR becomes a repetition of the universal test id of one order record (1 to 18 tests), and every OBR must carry the same specimen id, priority and order control. A message that is not (several patients or specimens, more than 18 tests, mixed values) is refused with a transform error, nothing is dropped or filtered.
Put your test codes in the tests table to translate the LIS code to the instrument's code; an unlisted code is sent as it is.
The instrument takes at most 18 tests selected per order record and refuses repeating the same test in one record; all OBR must also carry the same collection time and specimen type.
A specimen type other than serum or urine is left out, and the instrument uses its own.
mappings.evidence: Roche/Hitachi cobas e 411 Host Interface Manual v2.2 (Nov 2013), test order record cobas-type download: O-3 specimen id, O-5 ^^^code^dilution repeated with \, O-6 priority R or S, O-8 collection time, O-12 action code A, O-16 sample type 1/2/5, O-26 report type O; patient record P|1. Fixture is synthetic.
